title: THE VANTAGE POINT OF THE ELDERS: THE FATHERS HAVE SPOKEN

sense.text:
“And whilst they sinned not before their God, they prospered, because the God that hateth iniquity was with them.” The Israelites prospered because they were not in sin. That is what we need: a congregation of righteousness. When the bishops travel to the different schools, the congregations bring gifts, and they are appreciated, but the greatest gift the leadership is looking for is a sinless congregation. Given the choice between the two, give us a sinless congregation.

God “hateth iniquity.” If we know that God hates sin, why in the hell would we allow it among us while we are looking for blessings? That makes no sense. We want the Lord to prosper us, and we will prosper if there is no iniquity among us.

This is Leviticus 5:1, quoted on every page and every video we put out: it is time to execute it. You see some evil, you hear some evil, you report that damn thing, the hell with their feelings. Evil left sitting in the body will erode the spirits of everyone in it. It is not only in one school: the reports of fornication, adultery and lasciviousness are coming in from all the congregations, and at some point we have to put a stop to it.

“But when they departed from the way which he appointed them”: when we said we are not following God’s laws any more, took on all kinds of evil and left the Lord off to the side, “they were destroyed in many battles very sore.” If you are being destroyed, what blessing and prospering can you have? You cannot build anything, and we are trying to build beyond where we are.

We have people all around this building and this city, Gastonia, who hate the Israelites and hate what we are about: resurrecting our people from the dregs of society and setting our brothers and sisters up as princes and kings. The klan mentality of the surrounding cities does not want to see that. If we want God’s protection in the midst of those wolves, we had better do the right thing.

They “were led captives into a land that was not their’s, and the temple of their God was cast to the ground, and their cities were taken by the enemies.” We do not want that to happen to us. We are trying to make it into the kingdom as whole as we can. Through much tribulation we will make it, but we want to hold on to as many of our brothers and sisters as we can, and not do the things that cause the favour of the Lord to leave us. That is what sin does.

“Now therefore, my lord and governor, if there be any error...” That is the key. If there is any error, any sin, in these sanctuaries and schools, and we watch it and let the sinners beguile us into thinking it is righteous, that is crazy, and it is not going to happen.

“And they sin against their God, let us consider that this shall be their ruin.” This is what the nations are saying, the same nations in the cities around us, with the slave figurines in their yards. We do not want our ruin to be imminent; we want blessings. So any iota of evil, sin and wickedness, your job is to expose it, tell it, bring it forward. The men are to be the vanguards of righteousness, so that any spirit that comes in wanting to be evil sees the eyes on it and says those people are too strict. That is a compliment. We are looking for a few good men and a few good women.

The gospel is here to fix us in our sickness: all of us who come in, the bishop included, came in sick, and this sanctuary is the hospital, a safe haven to heal spiritual wounds. But whoever is not willing to be fixed, and wants to leave an egg of deception to hatch in the congregation and destroy what God is building, has to go.

“And let us go up, and we shall overcome them.” If we are in sin, the nations say they can overthrow us, because the God that hateth iniquity is not with us. Be at peace with all men if it be possible, but watch your surroundings, and the best protection we have is being in line with the Lord. That is the posture we must take as men, fathers, elders, sisters, mothers and wives: the vanguard of righteousness. We cannot entertain filth. This is grown folks business.

This begins the first part of the lesson, the mind of God, His vantage point, which is beyond our comprehension. The second part is our responsibility on this earth under His authority, and the third is holding fast to our diligence.

“And after these things I saw four angels standing on the four corners of the earth, holding the four winds of the earth, that the wind should not blow on the earth, nor on the sea, nor on any tree.” Visualize it. The four corners are where the militaries are, and the wind is not regular wind, because regular wind blows every day. The wind is destruction. The nations are itching to get at each other, ready to press the buttons, and the angels are holding them back from fighting.

Why are the angels holding it back? Because we have not gotten ourselves together as a nation. That is the love of the Most High: He has an elect He wants to make sure gets woken up. Say the number is at 143,999 and you are the last one. You think you are insignificant, but the Lord says hold those armies back until that one brother wakes up. He has whole armies stopped because of you, and many other things that have not yet dropped while you are being waited on.

We cannot fathom that kind of thinking, and we try to push God when we are not on that level. What you are responsible for is your own self, your own spirit and your own shenanigans. The Lord says get yourselves right, and He will take care of the rest.

The other angel has “the seal of the living God”, and the seal of the living God is the commandments, the law sealed among His disciples. He cried “to the four angels, to whom it was given to hurt the earth and the sea.” These angels’ job was to bring the destruction, and they were told to hold it back.

“Hurt not the earth, neither the sea, nor the trees, till we have sealed the servants of our God in their foreheads.” Do not bring the destruction yet. The sea is the battleships and the navies; all of that will be destroyed when Christ comes back and those armies are obliterated by Christ and the angels. The trees will be burned up when that fire comes.

That is the mission of this gospel: to seal up the elect, the 144,000. Sealed in their foreheads means in their minds, having their minds changed, until we repent. This part of the chapter speaks of the 144,000, who are men, righteous men; the sisters will be saved as well, coming on down the line.

“There were sealed an hundred and forty and four thousand of all the tribes of the children of Israel.” That is what this is about: sealing up the Israelites, the government of Israel that will set this whole planet in order. The 144,000 are the governing body of the kingdom, judges with the spiritual power to instantly get rid of anything that is not right. The Most High is tired of foolishness.

precepts.why:
“And after this I beheld, and, lo, there was gathered together a multitude of men, out of number, from the four winds of the heaven, to subdue the man that came out of the sea.” The four winds of Revelation 7:1 are the same four winds Ezra saw, and out of them comes a multitude of men gathered to fight the man that came out of the sea.

That is why the wind of Revelation 7 is not ordinary wind. It is the armies of the nations, the destruction, and the angels stand on the four corners holding them back. Picture the battlefield: the militaries straining to fight, and the hand of the Most High holding them until His elect are sealed.

sense.text:
The question always comes: when are we getting out of here? By right we want out. We pray every day, Lord, bring the destruction so we can get out of here, and the Lord says I am doing this when I am ready. We do not understand His timetable, because we only see our own point of view. He sees everything on this planet that has to come into the synchronicity He is looking for, and we cannot push Him.

“And give him no rest, till he establish, and till he make Jerusalem a praise in the earth.” That is what we are doing: we are not to give the Lord rest until He delivers us, establishes us and makes Jerusalem a praise in the earth.

But do we really want it? If we really wanted it, there would be no way we would entertain sin or allow evil right under our noses. Telling the Lord to hurry up while you are in sin, you mess around and get slain.

precepts.why:
Here is another one we say: make the time short, “remember the covenant, and let them declare thy wonderful works.” Lord, make the time short; remember the covenant You made with us. Let the nations know that You love us; tear these nations up and set us on high. That is the same cry as giving the Lord no rest.

But we are not on the Lord’s level. He will not be a millisecond late in sending His angels to destroy our enemies, but we do not know that time. In our wanting it, we must be in the right spiritual and mental space, so that when He sends the angels we are not caught off guard as by a thief in the night.

We want to declare His wonderful works with 100% confidence, not nervous that we might still be in some sin we have not found out yet. Examine yourselves to see if you be in the faith: that means the congregation examines itself, brothers and sisters looking at one another. People who say they do not need to congregate, that they can fellowship at home, do not want anyone to see their nasty, wicked evil. Come up in here and it will show, and righteous brothers and sisters will point it out. Accept that correction, because it is love: the wounds of a friend rather than the kisses of an enemy. That keeps you out of trouble and in the right space when the Lord does send the angels.

sense.text: “That man waxed strong with the thousands of heaven: and when he turned his countenance to look, all the things trembled.” That is Christ, and it is going to come. If Christ is coming back with that kind of power, you do not want Him showing up while you are into some foolishness. You do not want to be on the wrong side of that magnificent coming.

“And whensoever the voice went out of his mouth, all they burned that heard his voice, like as the earth faileth when it feeleth the fire.” That is how Christ is coming back. With that kind of power, do you think He will not see your wicked thoughts and your wicked actions, the things you thought you were hiding? He will see all of it.

“There was gathered together a multitude of men, out of number, from the four winds of the heaven, to subdue the man that came out of the sea.” The armies of the nations are setting up the fight against our deliverer. These nations do not want Christ to save us. They want us to remain in sin and evil, so that they can keep subduing and destroying the Israelites. We have to be smarter than that, brothers, and sisters, you have to make sure your diligence is on par too, because everybody is not right, and sisters get swept up in foolishness and end up down a dim road.

This is the same scene as Revelation 7. The Lord told the four angels to hold the four winds of the earth and not let them fight yet, because when Christ comes back these armies will try to fight against Him to keep us in slavery. Christ is coming back to destroy every last one of them, and if we are not right, He is going to destroy us too.

We say give the Lord no rest, make the time short, bring it on, but the Lord has His timetable, and when it is time for Him to move it, nobody can stop it. Esau will not be able to stop it.

“Therefore shall evil come upon thee”: upon Edom, upon our enemies. “Thou shalt not know from whence it riseth.” And the Lord’s enemies will include some of our own people, because they side with the nations and the oppressors. If you agree to be in sin to destroy your own people, you are working as an agent of the enemy. That is not about having a job with any agency; it is about spiritual and satanic business. What we have been dealing with in IUIC is negroes being wicked as hell, and negro here is a mind state, all twelve tribes of the northern kingdom, a mind state you were never supposed to have. You are the Israelites.

“And mischief shall fall upon thee; thou shalt not be able to put it off.” When the Lord says it is time, when all the planets have lined up, it is time to send Christ and the destroying angels and bring His people home, and you cannot stop it. If you are not ready, He comes as a thief in the night and you are caught off guard.

We are looking for a sign that we are near the prophecy, and we do know it. But first, the mind of the Most High: “Before the fair flowers were seen, or ever the moveable powers were established, before the innumerable multitude of angels were gathered together, Or ever the heights of the air were lifted up, before the measures of the firmament were named, or ever the chimneys in Sion were hot.” Before any of it was made, He had already considered it.

“Then did I consider these things, and they all were made through me alone, and through none other: by me also they shall be ended, and by none other.” The Most High made all of that, so we cannot question that kind of understanding. That is His vantage point.

And as they were made by Him alone, by Him alone they shall be ended. He is sending Christ when He is ready to send Christ.

precepts.why:
This goes deeper into the vantage point. We are trying to tell the Lord what to do, so the Lord clears the deck and lets everybody know where He stands. “Who hath directed the Spirit of the Lord, or being his counsellor hath taught him?” Nobody. These are questions for those of us trying to push Him, and we have no answer. Who counselled God? The dumb Christians talking about the way the Lord should be need to shut the hell up.

“With whom took he counsel, and who instructed him, and taught him in the path of judgment”: who told God you cannot love Jacob, you cannot hate Esau, you cannot forgive this one? “And taught him knowledge”: nobody. God is the knowledge; how are you going to teach Him? “And shewed to him the way of understanding?” God’s vantage point is well beyond the vantage point we think we have.

Having cleared it all up with qualifying questions nobody can answer, He proclaims what it is: “Behold, the nations are as a drop of a bucket.” All the nations put together equal one drop falling out of a big bucket of water; walking with a pail of water, you would not even notice it. They “are counted as the small dust of the balance”, not big dust, small dust on the scales, and dust weighs nothing. “He taketh up the isles as a very little thing”: the Polynesian and Hawaiian islands are nothing to Him.

“And Lebanon is not sufficient to burn, nor the beasts thereof sufficient for a burnt offering.” If they burned up all the beasts in Lebanon, it would not be sufficient for Him to accept the Arabs, Ishmael and all that, as His people. Only the Israelites are His people; that is why the chapter opens, Comfort ye my people.

“All nations before him are as nothing; and they are counted to him less than nothing, and vanity.” Less than nothing is spit; less than nothing is a bowel movement. That is what the nations are to God, and yet to Israel He says, comfort ye my people. The supreme power has it set up the way He wants it, and nobody can say anything against it. Ezra was quoting Isaiah, and in 2 Esdras 6 he says the same of the nations, that they are like spittle.

So it is the Lord alone who made all things, and the Lord alone who ends them. We cannot move His timetable.

sense.text:
There is a sign to let us know that it is near. We do not know the day or the hour, but we know we are in the season, and knowing these things are coming, what manner of persons ought we to be? We need to get our minds and spirits right.

“For, behold, the day cometh, that shall burn as an oven; and all the proud, yea, and all that do wickedly, shall be stubble.” If your mind and spirit are not right when that day comes, you are going to die. Woe unto them that desire the day of the Lord: what good is it to you when you are on the wrong side of the Lord? You will be howling, for the day of the Lord is at hand, and the destruction will come on those of us who are in evil and wickedness.

“The day that cometh shall burn them up”: the wicked, Israelites and all the nations. That is the same day spoken of in Revelation 7, when the nuclear fire comes from the missiles and the angels come with fire to burn everything up and purify the earth of its wickedness, so that a righteous new seed can be born: the nation of Israel in its repentance, ready to run the earth in righteousness. “It shall leave them neither root nor branch”: those are the trees of Revelation 7. It is the same exact incident.

“But unto you that fear my name shall the Sun of righteousness arise with healing in his wings”, and “ye shall tread down the wicked; for they shall be ashes under the soles of your feet in the day that I shall do this.” That is what is coming. All this destruction is on its way.

“Remember ye the law of Moses my servant, which I commanded unto him in Horeb for all Israel, with the statutes and judgments.” We know about what is going on in the Middle East, but we forget what is said right here. The statutes and judgments are the laws and commandments that keep us out of trouble, the same thing brought out in Judith: keep them, and they will keep the enemies at bay.

This is not speaking now of the law of sacrifice, but of the other commandments: thou shalt not steal, thou shalt not commit adultery, thou shalt not covet thy neighbour’s ox or his ass. Laws like that had to be given because of the negro mentality among our people, a mentality that is pervasive and that we need to get rid of, because you were not made that. Go to the root of the word negro: they will say it means black, but it also means dead, as in necro, necropolis, necrosis.

“Behold, I will send you Elijah the prophet before the coming of the great and dreadful day of the Lord.” This is the sign that we are near the end: the prophet brought this truth back, and that is how we know that we are the Israelites. This is the valley of the dry bones of Ezekiel 37: we are being rebuilt and brought back. Revelation says the same: their dead bodies lay in the street of the great city, spiritually called Sodom and Egypt, where they lied to us about Christ, three days and a half, and then the spirit of life from God entered into them, they stood up, and great fear fell on the enemies that saw them.

That is what is happening in these racist towns around us. We have committed no violence on anybody. We deal with everybody civilly, hold the doors for them, call the authorities to make sure they are all right. But our enemies want us to keep a wicked mentality, so they can accuse us to the Father and say, look at what they are doing.

“And he shall turn the heart of the fathers to the children.” The heart of the fathers is the Bible, the book of our fathers, and the spirit of the Lord coming through the prophets turns the mind of the fathers, this Bible, to the children: to us, the repentant ones coming into these sanctuaries, turning our minds back to our Bible. “And the heart of the children to their fathers”: our hearts and minds turned back to the Bible.

This is the title of the class: the fathers have spoken. In this Bible the fathers said what they said. When we rule in our congregations and set up rules, policies and orders, we go according to the word of our fathers, and when you go against that, you are going against the Most High. That is why what is bound on earth is bound in heaven: we are dealing with His word, not our own thoughts.

We set up programs to protect you, sisters and brothers. You are our sons and daughters. We have a vantage point over you that you do not have: we see the landscape of the whole congregation. A brother is upset because he cannot move as fast as he wants and wants to prove a sister; we say, brother, it is not time yet, work on yourself. We tell the sister, you are not ready yet, get yourself right. The daughter says, oh, he looks so cute; the father can tell this man is going to destroy her. The brother says, Lord, I have got to have her; the fathers say, you mess with that and you will be in trouble. The vantage point of the fathers is to protect you, so that when you do come together, things are right and we can bless it.

“Lest I come and smite the earth with a curse”: nuclear bombs. That is what Malachi was speaking of before the Lord wakes us up. The missiles are in the silos ready to rock. They did not exist when Malachi wrote, but they are here now, and Isaiah 34 speaks of the mushroom cloud. We now see what the prophets wrote, so we are that much closer to getting out of here, and we need to remember the laws and commandments and keep them, so that we are not caught off guard when that day comes.

precepts.why:
Malachi says the day “shall leave them neither root nor branch”, and the trees of Revelation 7 are those same trees. It is still talking about the same exact incident.

“And I saw another angel ascending from the east, having the seal of the living God”: the seal of the living God is the commandments, as Isaiah says, seal the law among my disciples. “He cried with a loud voice to the four angels, to whom it was given to hurt the earth and the sea.” Their job was to bring destruction. But He said do not do it yet, because He is still waking up His Israelite brothers and sisters.

“Hurt not the earth, neither the sea, nor the trees.” When that fire comes, the trees will be burned up; the sea is the battleships and navies, and all those armies will be obliterated by Christ and the angels. But not “till we have sealed the servants of our God in their foreheads”: until we repent, with our minds changed. The day that burns as an oven is held back until the elect are sealed.

Malachi warns, lest I “smite the earth with a curse”, and the curse is the destruction now sitting in the silos. It is at the doors, as Matthew 24 says. We are looking for a sign, and you will not get a bigger sign than that.

“Now learn a parable of the fig tree”: Christ is saying, pay attention to the seasons, watch the fig tree. “When his branch is yet tender, and putteth forth leaves, ye know that summer is nigh”: you know summer is near when you see how the trees are changing.

“So likewise ye, when ye shall see all these things, know that it is near, even at the doors.” That is where we are. The destruction is even at the doors, and here we are playing games. So we had better remember those laws and commandments and keep them, so that we are not caught off guard when that day comes.

sense.text:
Still dealing with the mind of God. “Then did I consider these things, and they all were made through me alone, and through none other”: nobody else did this but the Most High, and we are not on the level to question how He did things. “By me also they shall be ended, and by none other”: that is His smiting the earth with a curse.

We cannot move God’s timetable. We had better be ready when He decides to turn it on, because we do not know when all the gears are going to line up among the millions of things God has going on in this earth. He may say, I am not going to do this until that bird gets over Wyoming, and we do not understand the reason. Not a sparrow falls to the ground without your Father; the Lord is in the bird as well. And you try to move God with your hastiness, yet you will not even keep the commandments.

“What shall be the parting asunder of the times?” Give me the sign. “Or when shall be the end of the first”, the end of this wicked rule, “and the beginning of it that followeth?” The disciples asked the same question in Matthew 24: when shall these things be?

“From Abraham unto Isaac, when Jacob and Esau were born of him, Jacob’s hand held first the heel of Esau.” That is the only clue He gives, and the people in the churches do not even know who Esau is, so they are completely lost. Jacob’s hand holding the heel of Esau goes like cookies and milk with the class on the Achilles heel.

“For Esau is the end of the world.” Once we find out who Esau is, see how he acts on this earth and read about him in the Bible, we know that the time is near, even at the doors. Seeing that all these things shall be dissolved, what manner of persons ought we to be in holy conversation? Our minds need to be on that level, allowing nothing that jeopardizes that beauty and peace.

“And Jacob is the beginning of it that followeth.” Jacob is going to rule; that is the kingdom. When Esau, the great red dragon, is cast out of his rulership, that is the end of the world, and then comes salvation, strength and the kingdom of our God.

“The hand of man is betwixt the heel and the hand.” Betwixt means between: between the heel of Esau and the hand of Jacob are the other nations. They are insignificant. This whole planet operates on a pendulum that swings from Esau to Jacob, and everybody in between is affected by one or the other. They are never going to rule. It is either Esau, who is coming to his end, or Jacob ruling, and we are not losing the kingdom after this.

“O Lord that bearest rule, if I have found favour in thy sight, I beseech thee, shew thy servant the end of thy tokens.” That is what has been shown here: an idea of where we are in time. So we need to get our minds right.

precepts.why:
The same transition of time is recorded here. “And the great dragon was cast out”: that is Esau, the red dragon, the Romans. In the first verses of the chapter the great red dragon came into our heaven, meaning our kingdom, destroyed Jerusalem and cast us into captivity, and further down in the prophecy the Lord says He will destroy them.

Esau, the so-called white man, is cast out of his heaven, which is his rulership. People talk about Satan being kicked out of heaven while the Most High was building everything; that is not what happened. The heaven Esau falls from is his ruling kingdom right now, and that is what Isaiah 14 speaks of too. Satan cannot do anything without the Most High: in Job the Lord asks Satan where he came from and points him to Job, and Satan says he cannot touch him because of the hedge around him, the hedge we want around us. In the book of Kings an evil spirit offers to be a lying spirit in the mouth of Ahab’s prophets to persuade him to fall at Ramoth Gilead, and the Lord sends him. The Lord has control of everything.

“That old serpent, called the Devil, and Satan”: the old serpent going all the way back to Cain and to the beginning with Eve. Devil means evil; Satan means adversary. People mix those terms up. That is the white man, and he fits it to a tea. Like the elders said, he has never been white: not off-white, not beige. He is red, and that is his color. That is not hate; that is facts.

“Which deceiveth the whole world”: he made everybody on the planet believe Christ looks like Charles Manson, when the Bible describes Christ as a black man with woolly hair and feet like burned brass. That is great deception. “He was cast out into the earth, and his angels were cast out with him”: his angels are his missionaries, all his black preachers and ministers, imps of Satan to destroy our people. Christianity is the perfection of slavery. In slavery, whipped and in chains, we still wanted freedom; Christianity put us completely to sleep so that we do not even want to be free. It destroyed us from within.

When the Lord casts this devil down and smashes all those lies to smithereens, what happens next? “Now is come salvation, and strength, and the kingdom of our God, and the power of his Christ: for the accuser of our brethren is cast down, which accused them before our God day and night.” When these devils go down, we are going to rule and rejoice. That is Ezra’s sign: Esau is the end of the world, and Jacob is the beginning of it that followeth.

sense.text: Still the end time, and that day and hour knoweth no man. “I will stand upon my watch, and set me upon the tower, and will watch to see what he will say unto me”: Habakkuk was about to lay some heavy statements on the Most High. How long are we going to be in this captivity? He stands on his watchtower and demands answers, and waits to see how the Lord will answer him. That is how we talk now. “And what I shall answer when I am reproved”, because he knows the Lord is going to reprove him for questioning Him.

“Write the vision, and make it plain upon tables, that he may run that readeth it.” Write the vision down plain on the tables of the Bible. When the record is plain, they do not want to deal with it. That is why Christians run down the street when the Bible comes out: they are finding out that it is not about Christianity or any of the junk they are out there with.

“For the vision is yet for an appointed time.” We do not want to hear about an appointed time; we want to get out now. “But at the end it shall speak, and not lie”: when it does start speaking, we will feel it, it will be here, and nobody will be able to stop it or put it off. “Though it tarry, wait for it; because it will surely come, it will not tarry.” Habakkuk, Ezra, the disciples, everybody asking: do not worry, it is coming. Just be ready when it comes.

That is the kind of faith we need. Why would we play with sin, knowing our kingdom is coming?

“Behold, his soul which is lifted up is not upright in him”: that is Esau. His soul is of Satan, of the devil, the white man. “But the just shall live by his faith”: the just is us. We live by the faith of what the Most High said in this Bible, by the book of our fathers and its commandments.

“Remember this, and shew yourselves men”: now that we know what time we are in, show yourselves men. “Bring it again to mind”: be men and use your mind. God gave you a mind to envision greatness. You, the sons of God, are supposed to see things in your mind before you work your hands to build them. The Lord gave you that vantage point so that you can set up a congregation and make sure evil does not come among the brothers and sisters. “O ye transgressors”: change.

“Declaring the end from the beginning”: there is that heavy power again. God declared the end times before He said let there be light; He already had the end figured out. “And from ancient times the things that are not yet done”: everything is going to fall in its path the way the Lord wants it to fall. Think of the magnificence of the mind of the Most High. He declared from ancient times that a particular bird would fly over Wyoming on a certain day. You say that bird is insignificant; He says, I need that bird to do that, because it is connected to something else you do not know about. That is His vantage point. “My counsel shall stand, and I will do all my pleasure.”

“Calling a ravenous bird from the east”: there it is, a thing as insignificant as a bird. And while He calls that bird from the east, He calls “the man that executeth my counsel from a far country.” You and I are not on that level, and we are trying to move God.

“I have spoken it, I will also bring it to pass; I have purposed it, I will also do it.” He purposed that bird. You say it is just a bird, but the Lord has that bird up there for a reason; a sparrow does not fall to the ground unless the Most High causes it to fall. Everything is under His auspices. We cannot fathom why He told the angels to hold the armies back, but He knows. The only thing we need to do is obey what He said. From God’s vantage point, the calling of that bird is necessary in His overall plan.

“Let the wicked forsake his way”: those of us in wickedness need to forsake it. “And the unrighteous man his thoughts”: thoughts of lasciviousness, lust, adultery and fornication; get that out of your mind. “And let him return unto the Lord, and he will have mercy upon him; and to our God, for he will abundantly pardon.” He will pardon us if we are sincere, not pretending while doing evil on the back end and thinking nobody sees. The Lord understands the heartbeat of a raven, knows how many times a bird’s heart will beat in its whole life, and you think He does not see your black ass? You are playing with death.
“For my thoughts are not your thoughts, neither are your ways my ways, saith the Lord.” This shows the difference between God and us.

“For as the heavens are higher than the earth, so are my ways higher than your ways, and my thoughts than your thoughts.” The Lord looks down from the heavens on the whole planet and sees everything we cannot see. That is His vantage point. We are on earth, and the only vantage point we have is our immediate circumference. You cannot take that and tell the Lord what to do.

The same holds in the congregation. You may manage a department, and that is your vantage point; the leadership is over all the departments and sees the interactions between them, and why something happens here and not there. When we tell you what to do in your space, it is because we see the whole thing. As elders and leaders we are responsible for all of you, in your whole walk in this truth, and we watch for the things you do not yet see. The man on the tower sees the danger coming and blows the trumpet with a certain sound so the people behind him know what to prepare for, while they only see their own house.

“For as the rain cometh down, and the snow from heaven, and returneth not thither, but watereth the earth”, “So shall my word be that goeth forth out of my mouth: it shall not return unto me void, but it shall accomplish that which I please, and it shall prosper in the thing whereto I sent it.” Everything the Lord does has a purpose, that bird included, even when we do not understand it. We do not understand why He will send Christ back on whatever day and time, but when He does, it will all be perfect.

The same is done on the lower level in leadership. When we say brother, leave the sister alone, or tell a sister, leave the brother alone, there is a vantage point we see that you do not. We have no reason to interfere with your happiness; we want all of you to be happy. But if we see danger, we let you know, rather than you finding it out in judgment after you have laid with him. Do not rush. When you do things the right way, we can help you get to the next level, betrothal and the whole nine, and you have the blessing and counsel of the leadership through the trouble in the flesh that comes in any marriage. But if you said to hell with all of the steps, you were saying you have nothing to do with us.

precepts.why:
The Bible tells the leadership to take the oversight. The leaders, with the experience and the years they have been in the truth, see from a vantage point that younger men and younger women do not see. If we believe there is a God, and that Christ is the brain of this whole operation, then we are to trust the experience and understanding of the men He set up, because they see from a level we cannot see.

“Feed the flock of God which is among you, taking the oversight thereof”: listen to the wording. Oversight means a vantage point the flock cannot see. God gave these men revelation through the scriptures so that they can see how to guide you, and you have to trust that. Many brothers and sisters get horny and antsy, will not follow the counsel, and then come back asking the same leadership whose oversight they did not trust to counsel them after the fact. That is completely backwards; that is the negro mind.

“Not by constraint, but willingly”: the leaders willingly feed the flock and take the oversight, because they love their people. “Not for filthy lucre, but of a ready mind”: nobody is getting paid to do this. That is the oversight, the vantage point, of the fathers.

sense.text:
Now the second part: our responsibility on earth. We had better be ready as the Lord shortens the days. “And except those days should be shortened, there should no flesh be saved: but for the elect’s sake those days shall be shortened.” The Most High will wind things down. We claim we want the days shortened, but we are not ready for it, because wicked brothers are trying to slide in here.

Brothers and sisters who come into the truth from the world bring a world mentality, and the thing they would love most is to seduce and defile our men and our women. They do not want to change. They put on the fringes and the border of blue so that we let our guard down, then go behind the scenes to entice and allure you away from your protection. You want the days shortened while you have this kind of filth in your minds? The Most High is going to shorten them, and you had better be on the right side of that shortening.

“There shall arise false Christs, and false prophets, and shall shew great signs and wonders; insomuch that, if it were possible, they shall deceive the very elect.” A preacher on the internet tells women that marriage is not the goal and singleness is not the curse. That is the devil in black flesh. Why did God give a woman ovaries and breasts, and a man what he has, if she was never supposed to be married? It is not good for man to be alone. The eunuch who dedicated himself wholly to the Father did so because evil was so prevalent; when there is no wickedness among us and everything is in right order, there is no need for it. He does not care about eunuchs; he wants the women to stay in sin, laying with everybody, with their minds messed up. And he is married himself, flaunting his wife on the internet. That is backwards; that is the devil.

The very elect means the one third of us slated to make it. Evil is looking to knock you sisters and brothers off. Everybody with a border of blue and fringes is not right; do not be taken by a pretty beard. Give diligence and study, women and men both, so that you can recognize deception at your door, whatever it is wearing.

These lust-filled brothers can fake it, which is why the men are probed and checked out, and why, when a brother and sister come together the right way, they get their medical records and show them to each other. The leadership does not even ask to see them. All of it is to protect you.

The brothers who stand on the corner with fringes and a border of blue can break character quickly. A sister out in the world was approached by one who asked for her number, and she respectfully said no and asked him whether that was not against his own laws. A woman in the world knows more about the commandments than the man carrying the Bible, while sisters in here let men slide into their messages and entertain it. These whoremongering brothers look for women with a spinster’s anxieties, worried about getting old and not yet being married, and gas them up; to the whoremonger all bread is sweet.

Another man taught others to sleep with a woman at her own house first, fall asleep, and do it the night before she has to go to work, so that she leaves and he never leaves. The plan was never to love her; the plan was to get her place. He beds her in her own safe space so that she has no space left that he has not touched, and her mind is scrambled. This is not funny. Men are doing this to daughters, and fathers are responsible for women: there is no woman on this planet that a man is not responsible for at any time of her life, even a widow.

precepts.why:
Dinah in Genesis 34 was not raped. “And Dinah the daughter of Leah, which she bare unto Jacob, went out to see the daughters of the land.” She was not snatched; she went out on her own. With twelve mighty brothers, they surely tried to protect her and keep her in straitly and brought her the wisdom that pertains to a woman, and she did not want to hear it. She wandered away from the protection of her father and her brethren.

“And when Shechem the son of Hamor the Hivite, prince of the country, saw her, he took her, and lay with her, and defiled her.” Something had to be in her spirit to let him know. He knew who she was, and saw that she was not rolling in the spirit of her fathers or her brethren, and thought, I can have that. That is how slick brothers hit you sisters in the DM: they read your spirit, because you are not studying, and once they give you the tease talk, you feed right into it.

“And his soul clave unto Dinah the daughter of Jacob, and he loved the damsel, and spake kindly unto the damsel.” That is what tells you he did not rape her: he spake kindly to her. You gave him your ear, he got your underwear. She was enticed, beguiled, allured. Allure means to draw you from something into something else: away from your protection, from your fathers, from how you were brought up, from the protections the leadership puts around you. If sinners entice thee: enticing is not righteous; it is covetousness. She belonged to Jacob, and Shechem enticed her away and lay with her, then asked to marry her. You do not read anything else of her after that. Her brothers said, you are not staying in here, and took her out. That is the fathers utterly refusing: you already defiled her, you are not going to destroy her. She has to live with that stain, because she wandered out of her father’s care.

This is the kind of filth that comes in among the elect while we ask for the days to be shortened.

sense.text:
When you go behind the back of the fathers and elders to entice a daughter, that is evil as hell, and then you come in here and try to hit us with Exodus 22:16 without knowing that 17 is right behind it.

“Thou shalt not covet thy neighbour’s house.” Covet is not simply to desire; we desire many things without being covetous. To covet is to desire what belongs to another inordinately or culpably, and inordinate means against God’s laws: you want something and you violate God’s laws to get it. To take what belongs to someone else wrongfully, breaking the laws to get it: to entice a daughter is exactly that.

“Thou shalt not covet thy neighbour’s wife, nor his manservant, nor his maidservant, nor his ox, nor his ass, nor any thing that is thy neighbour’s.” Is the daughter, so to speak, the property of the father? Yes. Anything that is thy neighbour’s: the daughter belongs to him, the ox belongs to him, everything is under the father. If you go around him to get her, you enticed her away from that protection, and you never told the fathers or the elders.

A vantage point is a position that gives a good view or perspective. That is the vantage point the leadership has over our houses, our daughters and our sons. Whoever allures you away from the father’s protection has worked ill to his neighbour; it was done in wickedness. A man who whispers to you without your fathers and without the leadership does not have good intentions, and the fact that he did not do it the right way shows where his mind is. Sisters miss it because they are worried about not getting married, and a whole new generation of broken families and fatherless children comes from it.

A vantage point is a position that provides a clear, comprehensive or commanding view, often high, unobstructed or strategic. That is the leadership looking over the flock and seeing danger down the road you might not see. We know the games negroes run and the games sisters run, so we say, sister, change that behavior before you even think about marrying; brother, change that behavior. All of that is to protect you.

precepts.why:
Entice means to incite or instigate, to draw on by exciting hope or desire, to allure, as bait entices the fishes, often in a bad sense: to lead astray, to induce to evil, to tempt. And it is in the Bible: “My son, if sinners entice thee, consent thou not.”

That says in clear language that enticing is not righteous. It is trickery, deception, game, playing a game on you. A woman is not a toy and not a plaything; she brings forth children. To entice a daughter away from her father is to covet what is the neighbour’s.

The commandment says neighbour, and “Love worketh no ill to his neighbour.” If you say you love the sister, how in the world did you use ill means to get her? The law you broke is that you went around the father and around the leadership, which you were not supposed to do, and you enticed her and tricked her. That is wicked as hell.

She may think, with her mind scrambled, that they have love going on. But love worketh no ill to his neighbour: you would not have gone behind the father’s back and the leadership’s back to entice the woman and talk her out of her drawers, and then cover that violence by giving her scripture.

Give diligence, brothers and sisters. “Whereby are given unto us exceeding great and precious promises: that by these ye might be partakers of the divine nature, having escaped the corruption that is in the world through lust. And beside this, giving all diligence.”

As you come in here, you are supposed to be escaping the corruption of the world that comes through lust, truly repenting. When you look across the aisle, you are supposed to be looking for righteousness, not taking your sister for lust because of her behind, and the same goes on the other side.

That is what we say at our marriages: this is the day the Lord has made between you two; you can bring forth righteousness right here, and the Lord, the angels and everybody are in agreement with it. When you do things the right way, you have a whole community behind you.

Chapter 20 records the ten commandments, and from chapter 20 through 22 and beyond it speaks of wrongdoing. Chapter 22 opens with an ox being stolen: “If a man shall steal an ox, or a sheep, and kill it, or sell it; he shall restore five oxen for an ox.”

When a verse starts with if, you already know something is wrong. These are laws for when you have gone off from the commandments, did not listen to the law, and went beyond it, so a civil mandate had to be brought to keep you from being totally wicked.

Why must he restore five oxen for the one he stole? Because the father, the owner, was violated. Violence is physical force used to inflict injury, and it comes from the same root as violation. When you go behind the father’s back and entice the daughter, you have violated the father and the leadership, lured her away from her father’s protection. That is violence, a culpable violation: you broke the law. And then, after breaking the law, you pull up a scripture saying you did the right thing. That is how one covers violence with his garment.

sense.text:
“And if a man entice a maid that is not betrothed, and lie with her, he shall surely endow her to be his wife.” It begins with if: there are cases where this happens because of the negro mind. Everybody in the schools runs with this verse, and many congregations in the Israelite community use it to say they can entice women, lay with them, and then tell them they have to get married.

There is a distinction. Out in the world, it fits: the girl in the street does not have a father who knows better, and there is no leadership to go to. The least the man who lays with her can do is make her his wife, and when he finds her father, say, I lay with your daughter, and the least I can do is take her as my wife. That is why we teach that a brother who has laid with a woman in the world needs to marry her. There is nothing wrong with that.

But in here, where there are fathers and there is leadership, you go to the father first, before you even think of saying anything to that woman. To act as if the sisters are not cared for, as if there were no fathers and no leadership, is where the next verse comes into play.

The woman in the street corrected the Israelite because, whatever people think of us, we are looked at as knowing the Bible: you are breaking your own laws. That is embarrassing. Worse is a sister in the truth who lets a man lay with her and then comes to her fathers later to get the papers and try to make it right, when the woman in the world had the wisdom to say no. A boy in sixth grade sent a girl a note saying, I want your body, and she stood up and put him on blast before the teacher and the whole class. A sixth grader in the world had the sense to know he was not talking proper, and brothers in the body are doing the same thing while grown women let them talk them out of their drawers and think it is love.

“If her father utterly refuse to give her unto him”: the sisters in the world have no fathers to utterly refuse, but in here we do, because we have the vantage point of seeing where you are going to lead the sister. If you go around the father, that is violence against that man, and that is why five oxen are restored for one: restitution for the violation.

The father says, I do not know you, I did not approve this, she is my daughter, and I see that you are going to do her harm. That is the father’s vantage point, the same vantage point Jacob and the twelve brothers had. Simeon and Levi said, you are not taking her. Jacob asked why they had done all that destruction, and they answered that he had made a whore of their sister. Jacob feared the nations around would come down on small Israel, but they said, regardless, you cannot have her; we will risk it.

Utterly refuse means he is cursing, throwing things, he went and grabbed the shotgun. It is nicely written, but his head is on fire. Hell no: yes, my daughter was dumb enough to lay down with you, but I am not giving her to you. She will sit with that stain, and that will teach her to stay closed the next time somebody says something to her.

“He shall pay money according to the dowry of virgins.” He has to pay, and he still does not get the daughter. Somebody may say he paid, so he gets to take her; no. In another place in Deuteronomy it just says pay, and nothing else is heard because the father did not fight it. But if the father utterly refuses, she is not going anywhere. If it is up to the leadership, we are not signing it and not blessing it, because we see the danger. If she has an actual father, his decision overrides; many sisters have no contact with fathers in the world, and then the fathers in here make that decision.

precepts.why:
The same principle is written in Leviticus: “he shall restore that which he took violently away.” To entice that daughter, you violated the father, and that equates to violence: you took the daughter against the father’s wishes.

“Or the thing which he hath deceitfully gotten.” Was that out of deceit? Yes. Her fathers did not know anything about it, the leadership did not know anything about it, nobody knew, and when it was discovered by her sister, they still were not going to say anything. That is deceit. How can you come up later saying, here is the law? That is what Malachi 2:16 is speaking of.

“He shall even restore it in the principal, and shall add the fifth part more thereto, and give it unto him to whom it appertaineth.” The principal is the actual thing you took, and the fifth part is compounded on top of it. So you do not get the daughter, and you still have to pay the fathers. That is why judgment goes forward: we will not leave that kind of example for the rest of the sisters, for them to be beguiled and for a wicked brother to say he is applying Exodus 22:16. That is a damn lie.

“The Pharisees also came unto him, tempting him, and saying unto him, Is it lawful for a man to put away his wife for every cause?” Another negro law. Christ tells the Pharisees they are wicked as hell, because they are trying to use Moses’ law, Deuteronomy 24.

“Have ye not read, that he which made them at the beginning made them male and female”: the way God set it up from the beginning, there was no such thing as divorce. And here is a negro trying to quote Exodus 22:16. “For this cause shall a man leave father and mother, and shall cleave to his wife: and they twain shall be one flesh”: that is the way it is supposed to be, and that is what we teach in here. “What therefore God hath joined together, let not man put asunder.” God did not put these backdoor marriages together. That is why love worketh no ill to his neighbour: you will not do evil and call it love. You love nothing but your own lust.

“Moses because of the hardness of your hearts suffered you to put away your wives: but from the beginning it was not so.” The only reason Moses had to bring that law is that our people were hard-headed and giving Moses hell. It was written to keep negroes from being completely wicked, so that you cannot bring it up and say you are in righteousness. Those laws are failsafe laws: you are not supposed to be in any failure at all for them to be brought up. From the beginning it was not supposed to be that way, and here you are bringing in a failsafe law after you went off and did wrong. Watch yourselves, hold yourselves in the diligence of the scriptures, and study.

sense.text:
This is the verse that ends the madness of people doing evil behind everybody’s back and then, when caught, saying they were keeping the commandments. “For the Lord, the God of Israel, saith that he hateth putting away.” The subject was the priests putting away their wives, wickedness among the priests that the prophet had to check.

“For one covereth violence with his garment.” Violence is equal to violation, as brought out with Exodus 22. The garment has the borders and the fringes, and the fringes represent the laws. So he did evil, and then covers it with a failsafe law, giving the sister a so-called law from the Bible to say they are correct. You step past the fact that you deceived to get her: you covered violence and said you were in the scriptures, and sisters get caught like that.

“Therefore take heed to your spirit, that ye deal not treacherously.” The violence is dealing treacherously with the wives while saying we are in the scriptures. That is what covering it up means: bringing these negro laws to say we are all right.

“Ye have wearied the Lord with your words.” The Lord says, I see your BS; you have wearied Me with your lies, even though you used a scripture. Many people are not catching this. “Yet ye say, Wherein have we wearied him?” They answer back, where have we wearied the Lord? We have Exodus 22:16; that is in the Bible. Wherein have we wearied the Lord, when we are keeping the commandments?

“When ye say, Every one that doeth evil is good in the sight of the Lord.” We weary the Lord when we call evil good. The evil was enticing the sister, and covering it up by saying you are using the law, using the words of the Bible against righteousness to take the daughter from the father. That is wicked as hell. If a man violated a father on that level, that father would never want to see him again.

This is a warning: do not get caught in any more foolishness. The leadership has approved instituting it across the groups: no more backdoor marriages. Courting is to be done the old way, in plain view, as it once was on the front porches under the watchful eyes of the parents and the neighbours, where there was no sneaking, a young man earned the family’s approval before the woman’s hand, and the community knew what was being dealt with. There is no enticement in that. You covered the violence of violating the fathers, enticing the daughter away from her protection to lay with her, and then used a negro law to say you were in the Bible: that is violence covered with the garment, the long fringes the Pharisees wore. They were hypocritical as hell, just like the men who deal with you women this way, and the women who deal with the men the same way. Both of you watch out.

precepts.why:
What does the garment mean? “The scribes and the Pharisees sit in Moses’ seat: All therefore whatsoever they bid you observe, that observe and do; but do not ye after their works: for they say, and do not.” These are the same men who tempted Christ in the 19th chapter with a failsafe law, when Christ took them all the way back to the beginning: there would be no need for a failsafe law if you were keeping the commandments of God.

“For they bind heavy burdens and grievous to be borne, and lay them on men’s shoulders; but they themselves will not move them with one of their fingers. But all their works they do for to be seen of men: they make broad their phylacteries, and enlarge the borders of their garments.” The borders of the garment carry the fringes, and the fringes represent the laws.

So when a man covers violence with his garment, he covers his violation with the law: he did evil and holds up the law to say he is correct, just as the Pharisees enlarged their borders to be seen of men. You sisters have to be smart. The sixth grader was smart; the sister in the car was smart; you must be beyond all of that.

When they say, wherein have we wearied the Lord, this is what they are talking about. “When a man hath taken a wife, and married her, and it come to pass that she find no favour in his eyes”: he does not desire her any more. “Because he hath found some uncleanness in her”: some uncleanness could be anything. She burnt the eggs, she did not iron his clothes right, she put his shoes in the wrong place. Men were finding reasons to get rid of their wives for BS reasons, and that is what Christ was dealing with in Matthew 19.

“Then let him write her a bill of divorcement, and give it in her hand.” On a bill of divorce the man writes the grounds for putting her away: fraud, adultery, abandonment, thievery, whatever it is. It is put in her hand so that the next man knows why she is not with her husband. That is a stain that goes on her.

Sisters, do not play around with this. Get the man properly and you do not have to go through this. Play games, and you get stained.
